Plant names, and the names of things you add, are in Title Case everywhere: Black-Eyed Susan, Arbor or Pergola. A name you typed stays as you typed it.
In a plant's details, each fact comes first and stands out; its source follows, smaller, as "Source: NC State". The "confirmed" and "one source" endings are gone.
The garden location sheet starts with the ZIP code and what it's for. How your ZIP is used, and the sources, are folded under the lookup.

The poison filters say it one way: "Hide plants toxic to people", "… to dogs", "… to cats", "… to horses", each with what it hides, according to NC State. Plants are marked "Toxic to people" and "Toxic to dogs" the same way.
"Anyone you need to protect?" now just says it hides plants that are toxic to them.
Plainer words for new gardeners: "width when grown" in place of "mature spread" or "spread", and everyday words for leaf shapes and flower clusters in a plant's details.
On a phone's browser, a card explains, once, what installing the app on your home screen means and how to do it. It's in Help too.
A plant's details have "See photos", which opens a web image search for it in a new tab.
